reviews.comment: The class is very straight forward, three exams, nothing else. The first two exams are insanely easy, just work through the problem sets he posts and you'll do fine. The hardest part of this entire course was algebra, if you spend a couple hours before each exam knowing the algebra like the back of your hand you will be good. Pretty chill guy too.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honors section graded on 2 exams & final (non-cumulative). Generous grading policy w/ 80-100 being an A. 5 pts free on exams & final. If you know how to do the practice questions (which have a key), you'll do fine. Literally just review slides and practice questions. Will answer questions in class, but sometimes ppl were still confused after.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have taken at A&M Professor bento makes it as hard on you as possible, he does not give a topic sheet before exams, when he posts solutions to problems he only posts the answers and they are very long algebra heavy problems so it leaves you to figure everything out on your own, do yourself a favor and don't take his class

He goes very slow in class, so if you read on your own may not need to attend class. First half of this course is similar to microeconomic theory and you will use a lot of the same math. Do the problem sets and previous year question papers and it's an easy A. The textbook is really helpful but if you want cover the material fast look up youtube.

The grading scale is weighted to 100-80 = A, 79-70 = B, etc. Only have 3 tests (usually 2 problems with 2-3 subparts each). I didn't go to the lectures, but just studied the practice problems and lecture problems (those he does in class so attend or get a friend to attend for you). Overall, easy class since only 3 tests.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are pretty boring, but are quite essential to understanding how to solve the problems he gives on exams. He posts slides (which aren't helpful) but not the solutions to the problems he solves in-class (which are very similar to exam questions). Only grades off of 3 exams but the cutoffs for each letter grade are lower.

Avoid at all costs. He won't meet outside of office hours even if you have a conflict.  Will smoke and do other things while you are trying to talk to him.   Doesn't appear to care about students. Not sure why he decided to be a professor.  Worst professor I have ever had.

He's patient and very accessible even outside of the classroom.

Although not  the most engaging, he makes the effort to carry the class along.

He's fine with being interrupted at any time during his lecture for clarification.

You'd need to pay attention during his class, as he takes time to explain the practical aspects of the concepts.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the worst I have taken an economics course with...basically a self taught class with no homeworks only exams
Hardly any of the test material is taught in class.  Provides little to no solutions to homeworks, and if he does he will put little to no explanation to the answers he provides.
Worst class you would ever imagine. Professor doesnt have a logic path on what he is covering. His lecture easily put everyone into a good afternoon nap.

I can tell Bento is a decent guy but the class is pretty tough as it is. 100-80 is an A, 79-70 is a B. He did listen to his students by uploading more in depth solutions at the end of the course but overall seemed annoyed at the online format of the class, which I understand would be hard to switch to. He gets irritated easily but is generally nice
Structure of this class is terrible. exams are "based" on the problem sets swapped with twists and turns along with different wording. Sooo you kinda have to teach yourself the content instead

Very knowledgeable professor, but this class is hard. Grade is based on only 3 tests, so if you bomb the first one your A is pretty much gone. He lectures based on the book, but doesn't really solve practice problems in class, which is what the tests are based off of. You have to do a lot of self teaching and the book is really helpful
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures can get very boring and they are based only on the textbook. He posts practice questions before tests with the answers that helped a lot for the exams and a lot of the questions were the same.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best and worst thing is the tests. Best because homework is kept to a minimum (problem sets that are apparently supposed to help with the tests) and worst because they are difficult and comprise your entire grade. He likes to digress from his lecture material on exams making it a roll of the dice as to what material you'll see.
reviews.ratingTags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY
